# Adjudication Task — Chapter 317

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃317화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“아.”
  6|
  7|깜빡이는 긴 속눈썹 위로 햇살이 부서진다. 주화란은 잠에서 깬 후에도 침상에 누운 채 한참이나 천장을 바라보았다.
  8|
  9|어젯밤, 그녀와 용봉표국은 마침내 서안에 닿을 수 있었다.
 10|
 11|천력부가 이끄는 흑석채는 이번 표행의 마지막 장애물이었다.
 12|
 13|그들은 안전한 번화가를 지나 서안의 후미진 객잔에 행낭을 풀었다. 객잔에는 침상은 물론 따뜻한 음식과 목욕물이 모두를 기다리고 있었다.
 14|
 15|주화란은 모든 표물을 빠짐없이 점검한 다음 쓰러지듯 잠이 들었었다.
 16|
 17|‘드디어 끝이 보이는구나.’
 18|
 19|이곳은 안전하다. 산길을 막아서는 산적도, 정체를 숨기고 무리 지어 습격하던 낭인들도 없다. 이번 표행의 주목적이었던 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)을 종남파에 넘기기만 하면 끝이다.
 20|
 21|용봉표국은 노력에 합당한 보상을 받을 것이고 모두 함께 집으로 돌아갈 것이다.
 22|
 23|서른세 개의 유골함과 함께.
 24|
 25|‘서른셋…….’
 26|
 27|주화란의 눈동자가 문득 희미하게 깜빡였다.
 28|
 29|서른세 개의 유골함, 서른세 사람의 얼굴, 그들과 울고 웃었던 기억이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
 30|
 31|“아, 이러면 안 되는데…….”
 32|
 33|옷소매로 눈가를 문지른 주화란이 자신을 두 뺨을 강하게 쳤다. 짝! 하는 소리와 함께 흐트러진 정신이 조금이나마 돌아온다.
 34|
 35|“이제 시작이야. 정신 똑바로 차려야 해.”
 36|
 37|표행은 아직 끝나지 않았다.
 38|
 39|종남파와 약조한 기한까지는 사흘이 남았고, 그 안에 천년설삼을 무사히 전달해야만 표행이 끝난다.
 40|
 41|“그리고…… 새로운 시작이 되겠지.”
 42|
 43|주화란은 작은 목소리로 중얼거리며 품 안을 더듬었다. 단단히 밀봉된 목곽(木槨)을 꺼내어 확인한 뒤에 다시 집어넣어 끈으로 고정했다.
 44|
 45|단지 그것만으로도 시원한 향기가 코끝을 맴돌다가 이내 사라졌다.
 46|
 47|무림인이라면 누구나 바라마지 않는 천고의 영약, 천년설삼이 목곽 안에 들어 있었다.
 48|
 49|“흐트러지지 말자, 주화란. 이제 겨우 한 걸음이야.”
 50|
 51|주화란이 스스로를 향해 다짐하던 그때였다.
 52|
 53|“화란아, 일어났느냐?”
 54|
 55|문밖에서 들려온 익숙한 목소리. 옷매무새를 다듬은 주화란이 대답했다.
 56|
 57|“네, 허 숙부. 들어오셔도 돼요.”
 58|
 59|“그럼 잠시 실례하마.”
 60|
 61|잠시 후, 문을 열고 들어온 총표두 허준이 밝은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
 62|
 63|“예정보다 빨리 표국으로 돌아갈 수 있게 되었다.”
 64|
 65|“그 말씀은…….”
 66|
 67|“종남파가 서안에서 기다리고 있다는구나.”
 68|
 69|“종남파가요?”
 70|
 71|“그래. 그것도 태을무정검(太乙無情劍)이 직접 왔다고 들었다, 하하하.”
 72|
 73|웃음을 머금은 허준과는 달리, 주화란의 눈빛은 깊게 가라앉았다.
 74|
 75|‘종남파가, 그것도 태을무정검이 서안까지 직접?’
 76|
 77|귀환이 앞당겨졌으니 원래라면 허준처럼 기뻐해야 하는 것이 맞다.
 78|
 79|하지만 지금까지 종남파가 보여 온 오만무례한 태도를 생각할수록, 마음 깊숙한 곳에서 불안감이 스멀스멀 올라왔다.
 80|
 81|“허 숙부, 뭔가 이상하지 않아요?”
 82|
 83|“응? 이상하다니, 무엇이 말이냐?”
 84|
 85|“예정된 기간까지는 아직 사흘이나 남았어요.”
 86|
 87|“사흘밖에 안 남은 거지. 서안에서 종남산까지는 천천히 이동해도 이틀이면 충분하다.”
 88|
 89|“숙부께서 종종 그러셨죠. 무림에는 우연이 없다. 무슨 일이 벌어지더라도 이상하지 않은 곳이 무림이라고.”
 90|
 91|“화란아, 무슨 말이 하고 싶은 게냐?”
 92|
 93|도무지 이해가 되지 않는다는 듯한 허준의 눈빛에 주화란이 무겁게 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“지금까지 종남파는 우리 용봉표국을 은연중에 적대해 왔습니다. 이번 표행이 실패하는 걸 누구보다 원하고 있을 거예요. 일부러 어려운 조건을 내걸었던 이유도 그 때문이고요.”
 96|
 97|“하지만 받아들였지. 훌륭하게 해냈고.”
 98|
 99|종남파가 요구한 조건은 까다로운 것이었다. 오죽하면 종남파의 이름에 혹해서 몰려든 다른 표국주들조차 고개를 절레절레 내저으며 의뢰를 포기했을 정도다.
100|
101|그들이 원하는 기한 내에 천년설삼을 운송해 주지 못하면, 표행은 실패로 돌아가고 천문학적인 금액을 위약금으로 물어내야 하니까.
102|
103|하지만 주화란은 고심 끝에 종남파의 의뢰를 받아들였다.
104|
105|이유는 단 하나, 용봉표국의 비상(飛上)을 위해서였다.
106|
107|‘그리고 큰 희생을 치러야 했지.’
108|
109|일어나지 말아야 할 일이 일어났다.
110|
111|천년설삼에 관한 정보가 유출된 것이 원인이었다.
112|
113|주화란은 바보가 아니다. 아직은 경륜이 부족할 뿐, 모든 가능성을 열어 두고 생각할 줄 아는 명석한 두뇌의 소유자였다.
114|
115|지금까지 마음속에만 담아 두었던 의심이 서서히 실체를 갖추는 기분이다. 주화란은 조용히 입을 열었다.
116|
117|“어쩌면, 어쩌면 종남파가…….”
118|
119|“그만.”
120|
121|주화란의 말을 가로막은 허준의 얼굴은 딱딱하게 굳어 있었다.
122|
123|“그만하거라. 네가 지금 무슨 생각을 하고 있는지 모르는 바가 아니나, 그 이상은 터무니없다. 아니, 위험하기까지 해.”
124|
125|“하지만.”
126|
127|“종남파에 관한 소문은 익히 알고 있다. 그들이 자신들의 표국을 키우기 위해 우리를 견제하고 있다는 것도 사실이지. 하지만 지금 화란이 네가 말하려는 것은…… 위험한 억측이야.”
128|
129|“허 숙부…….”
130|
131|“숙부로서, 용봉표국의 총표두로서 부탁하마. 너와 표국을 위험에 빠트리지 말아라.”
132|
133|비록 피 한 방울 섞이지 않은 남이지만, 그녀의 어린 시절부터 늘 따뜻하게 대해 주었던 의숙부다.
134|
135|그런 그가 작심한 듯 굳은 얼굴로 말을 쏟아내자 주화란은 더 이상 종남파에 관한 말을 이을 수 없었다.
136|
137|“후우.”
138|
139|작게 한숨을 내쉬는 주화란의 어깨를 허준이 따뜻하게 감싸 안았다.
140|
141|“말이 심했다면 미안하구나.”
142|
143|“아니에요. 제가 좀 과민했나 봐요.”
144|
145|“그럴 만도 하지. 종남파가 안 하던 짓을 했으니. 당주나 총관도 아닌 태을무정검을 보낼 줄이야.”
146|
147|종남파 장문인의 두 사형 중 한 사람.
148|
149|늘 본산에 머무르며 두문불출하는 태을무정검을 사람들이 오랫동안 기억하는 이유는 간단했다.
150|
151|‘종남제일검(綜南第一劍).’
152|
153|종남파가 배출해 낸 초절정 고수. 천하삼십육검의 극의를 이뤘다고 알려진 무시무시한 검공의 소유자가 바로 태을무정검이었다.
154|
155|장문인인 풍운검군에 비견될 만한 거물이 직접 나선 것에는 분명 큰 의미가 있을 터였다.
156|
157|주화란은 그것이 가장 의문이었다.
158|
159|“도대체 왜 하필 태을무정검일까요?”
160|
161|“마음이 급해서겠지. 종남이 천금을 들여 천년설삼을 구했던 이유가 노호검객의 내상 때문이니 말이다. 하나뿐인 사형이 그리되었으니 그 속이 오죽하겠느냐?”
162|
163|일견 듣기에는 타당한 말이다.
164|
165|그러나 주화란은 수년 전, 아버지인 주호군에게 들었던 말을 똑똑히 기억하고 있었다.
166|
167|‘무서운 사람이라고 하셨지.’
168|
169|그녀의 아버지는 군자검이라 불릴 정도로 인자한 사람이었다. 사람 보는 눈이 관대한 주호군이 그리 말할 정도라면 태을무정검은 그의 검공만큼이나 날카로운 인물이 분명했다.
170|
171|‘마지막까지 방심하지 말자.’
172|
173|생각을 정리한 주화란이 허준에게 물었다.
174|
175|아직 마음에 걸리는 한 사람을 향한 질문이었다.
176|
177|“송 표두는 어떻던가요?”
178|
179|“아, 그게 말이다.”
180|
181|잠시 머뭇거리던 허준이 대답했다.
182|
183|“믿을 만한 표사들을 시켜 밤낮으로 은밀히 지켜보고 있었는데, 화란이 너도 알다시피 어젯밤은 모두 긴장이 풀리는 바람에…….”
184|
185|“시선을 뗐군요.”
186|
187|“면목이 없구나. 더 신경 쓰지 못한 내 잘못이다.”
188|
189|멋쩍게 시선을 피하는 허준의 모습에 주화란은 작게 한숨을 내쉬었다.
190|
191|“하아…….”
192|
193|출신도 명확하지 않고 세간의 평가도 좋지 않은 송일섬은 주요 감시 대상이었다.
194|
195|특히 진태경을 만난 직후부터는 그를 향한 의혹이 짙어지고 있었다.
196|
197|‘잘 지켜보라고 그렇게 신신당부했는데.’
198|
199|허준은 분명 좋은 사람이다. 삼십여 년을 용봉표국에 몸담으며 주호군과 호형호제할 정도로 가까운 사이기도 했다.
200|
201|하지만 지금처럼 종종 보여 주는 허술한 면모들이 크고 작은 실수를 불러오기도 했다.
202|
203|‘이번만큼은 그러지 않기를 바라는 수밖에.’
204|
205|이미 엎질러진 물. 어차피 천년설삼은 그녀의 품 안에 있다.
206|
207|주화란은 실망스러운 기색을 감추고 입을 열었다.
208|
209|“종남파가 어디에서 접선하자고 하던가요?”
210|
211|“서안에서 서쪽 끝에 있는 등왕루라는 다루(茶樓)에서 정오까지 만나자고 하더구나.”
212|
213|등왕루라면 주화란도 간혹가다가 들렀던 유명한 다루다.
214|
215|보는 눈도 많고 분위기도 조용하니 표행을 마무리 짓기에는 안성맞춤인 곳이었다.
216|
217|“일각 후에 출발할 테니 준비해 주세요.”
218|
219|
220|
221|* * *
222|
223|
224|
225|백무성이 서안루로 찾아온 것은 한창 짐을 싸고 있던 때였다.
226|
227|“정말 바로 떠나십니까?”
228|
229|“저도 며칠 더 묵고 싶긴 한데, 아시다시피 일정이 좀 빡빡하네요.”
230|
231|“아쉽군요. 가능하다면 본산에 모시고 싶었는데.”
232|
233|“돌아오는 길에 들를게요. 그때 화산 구경이나 한번 시켜 주세요.”
234|
235|“하하, 걱정하지 마십시오. 제가 책임지고 제대로 구경시켜 드리겠습니다.”
236|
237|또 나왔다. 풀코스 발언.
238|
239|사실 풀코스는 기대도 안 한다. 다음에 만날 때는 이번처럼 누군가와 박 터지게 싸우고 있지만 않기를 바랄 뿐이다.
240|
241|그러다가 문득, 호탕하게 웃는 백무성의 얼굴을 빤히 바라보며 생각했다.
242|
243|‘말이라도 꺼내 봐야 하나. 용봉표국과 종남파에 관해서.’
244|
245|잠시 고민하던 그때 백무성이 얼굴을 더듬으며 물었다.
246|
247|“왜 그러십니까? 혹시 제 얼굴에 뭐가 묻기라도.”
248|
249|“…….”
250|
251|“진 소협?”
252|
253|“아, 아닙니다. 그냥 잠깐 다른 생각이 들어서.”
254|
255|시벌, 모르겠다.
256|
257|어차피 종남파나 용봉표국이나 따지고 보면 내게는 생판 남일 뿐이다. 어떤 분쟁이 있더라도 그들끼리 해결해야 할 문제.
258|
259|지금 내 코가 석 자인데 이런 문제까지 신경 쓰는 건 괜한 오지랖이다.
260|
261|‘여긴 무림이니까.’
262|
263|나는 내심 중얼거리며 적천강을 지게에 앉혔다. 그리고 모피를 집어 하나씩 그 위에 올리기 시작했다.
264|
265|그러는 와중에도 왜 주화란이 생각나는지 모르겠다.
266|
267|스치듯이 보고 지나친 송일섬이라는 놈도 함께.
268|
269|‘지금 생각해 보면 수상쩍은 놈이었어. 궁기방보다 더 구린내가 풍겨.’
270|

[P30]

[P31]
“We’ll be able to return to the Escort Bureau sooner than expected.”

[P32]
“You mean…”

[P33]
“The Zhongnan Sect is waiting in Xi’an.”

[P34]
“The Zhongnan Sect?”

[P35]
“That’s right. And I hear the Taeeul Merciless Sword himself has come. Hahaha.”

[P36]

[P40]
“Uncle Heo, don’t you think something is strange?”

[P41]
“Hm? What do you mean?”

[P42]
“There are still three days until the agreed-upon deadline.”

“Only three days. Even traveling slowly, it takes no more than two to get from Xi’an to Mount Zhongnan.”

“You used to say it all the time, Uncle. There are no coincidences in the Murim. It’s a place where nothing should surprise you, no matter what happens.”

“Hwaran, what are you trying to say?”

Under Heo Jun’s utterly baffled gaze, Ju Hwaran spoke gravely.

[P52]

[P53]
*And we had to pay a terrible price for it.*

[P54]
Something that should never have happened had happened.

[P55]
Information about the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng had been leaked.

[P56]

[P58]
“Perhaps… perhaps the Zhongnan Sect…”

[P59]
“Enough.”

[P61]

[P62]
“But—”

[P63]

[P64]
“Uncle Heo…”

[P65]

[P67]

[P68]
“Phew.”

[P70]
“I’m sorry if I was too harsh.”

[P71]

[P72]
“You had reason to be. The Zhongnan Sect did something it had never done before. Who would have expected them to send the Taeeul Merciless Sword instead of a Hall Master or Chief Steward?”

[P73]
The Taeeul Merciless Sword was one of the Zhongnan Sect Leader’s two Senior Brothers.

[P74]

[P75]
*The First Sword of Zhongnan.*

[P76]

[P77]
There had to be great significance behind a figure comparable to the Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, personally stepping forward.

[P78]

[P79]
“Why the Taeeul Merciless Sword, of all people?”

[P80]

[P83]
*He said the man was frightening.*

[P85]
*I can’t let my guard down until the very end.*

[P86]

[P87]
“What about Captain Song?”

[P88]
“Ah, about that…”

[P89]

[P90]
“I had trustworthy escorts watching him discreetly day and night, but as you know, everyone relaxed last night…”

[P91]
“You took your eyes off him.”

[P92]
“I have no excuse. It was my fault for failing to keep a closer watch.”

[P93]
As Heo Jun awkwardly avoided her gaze, Ju Hwaran let out a small sigh.

[P94]
“Haa…”

[P95]
Song Ilseom, whose origins were unclear and whose reputation was poor, had been one of their primary surveillance targets.

[P96]
Her suspicions of him had grown particularly strong after their encounter with Jin Taekyung.

[P97]
*I told him over and over to keep a close eye on Song Ilseom.*

[P98]
Heo Jun was certainly a good man. He had served the Yongbong Escort Bureau for more than thirty years and had been close enough to Ju Hogun for them to address each other as brothers.

[P99]

[P100]
*All I can do is hope it doesn’t happen this time.*

[P101]
The milk had already been spilled. In any case, the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was safely in her possession.

[P102]

[P103]
“Where did the Zhongnan Sect ask us to meet?”

[P104]
“At a teahouse called Tengwang Pavilion on the western edge of Xi’an. They want us there by noon.”

[P105]
Tengwang Pavilion was a famous teahouse Ju Hwaran had visited a few times herself.

[P106]
There would be plenty of witnesses, and the atmosphere was quiet, making it the perfect place to conclude an escort mission.

[P107]
“We’ll leave in fifteen minutes. Please prepare.”

[P108]
* * *

[P109]
Baek Museong came to Xi’an Tower while we were in the middle of packing.

[P110]
“Are you really leaving right away?”

[P111]
“I’d like to stay a few more days too, but as you know, our schedule is a little tight.”

[P112]
“That’s unfortunate. If possible, I would have liked to escort you to the main sect.”

[P113]
“I’ll stop by on the way back. Give me a tour of Huashan then.”

[P114]
“Haha, don’t worry. I’ll take responsibility for showing you everything properly.”

[P115]
There it was again. The full-course treatment.

[P116]

[P117]
Then, as I stared at Baek Museong’s face while he laughed heartily, a thought occurred to me.

[P118]
*Should I at least mention it? The Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect.*

[P119]
While I was debating, Baek Museong touched his face and asked,

[P120]
“Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something on my face?”

[P121]
“…”

[P122]
“Young Hero Jin?”

[P123]
“Oh, no. Something else just crossed my mind.”

[P124]
*Shit, I don’t know.*

[P125]
When you got right down to it, the Zhongnan Sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau were both complete strangers to me. Whatever dispute they had was theirs to resolve.

[P126]
I already had more than enough problems of my own. Worrying about this too would just be sticking my nose where it didn’t belong.

[P127]
*This is the Murim, after all.*

[P128]
I muttered inwardly as I seated Jeok Cheongang on the pack frame. Then I picked up the furs and began piling them over him one by one.

[P129]
Even as I worked, I couldn’t understand why Ju Hwaran kept coming to mind.

[P130]
Song Ilseom, whom I had only glimpsed in passing, came to mind along with her.

[P131]
*Now that I think about it, he was a suspicious bastard. He stank even worse than Gung Gibang.*

[P132]
After learning about the relationship between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect, I found myself wondering who that bastard really was.

[P133]
His Level was a staggering 110. At that level, he could probably strip one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes clean to the bone.

[P134]
He had looked to be in his early to mid-thirties at most, but… who was he, and which sect did he belong to?

[P135]
*Could he be an assassin sent by the Zhongnan Sect? No, that’s probably going too far.*

[P136]
Had he simply fallen for Ju Hwaran’s beauty and decided to stay?

[P137]
No. If that were the case, he’d have no reason to conceal his true abilities. Was this one of those stories where the protagonist hides his power? Did a loser look cooler rescuing someone if he had been hiding his strength all along?

[P138]
*Ju Hwaran. We only exchanged a few words, but she seemed like a good person. She had a refreshingly direct way of speaking too.*

[P139]
Her martial talent was extraordinary as well. She had reached the Peak realm at her age.

[P140]
And then there was… right. The dimples that appeared when she smiled were pretty. So were her half-moon eyes.

[P141]
*Come to think of it, she looked like a cat.*

[P142]
Cats had always been my favorite animals.

[P143]
“Um, Squad Leader?”

[P144]
“Hm? Yeah?”

[P145]
I turned and saw Hyuk Mujin staring at me strangely.

[P146]
And not just him. Gung Gibang, Cheongpung, and even Baek Museong were all looking at me the same way.

[P147]
“What? Why is everyone staring at me?”

[P148]
“Well, the thing is…”

[P149]
Hyuk Mujin cautiously pointed at the pack frame.

[P150]
“In my humble opinion, Great Hero Jeok is going to suffocate at this rate.”

[P151]
“Gasp!”

[P152]
I hurriedly flung aside the furs that had piled up like a mountain.

[P153]
Jeok Cheongang, who had nearly gone to meet that person while still in a coma, was breathing faintly.

[P154]
“Oh, Benefactor! You’re just like me!”

[P155]
“Did you just insult me?”

[P156]
“Ah. No, no. That isn’t what I meant…”

[P157]
Ignoring Cheongpung as he instantly drooped, I began piling the furs back on. Jeok Cheongang’s slight frame quickly disappeared beneath them.

[P158]
Only after making sure enough air could pass through did I hoist the pack frame onto my back.

[P159]
“All right. If everyone’s ready, let’s get going.”

[P160]
We stepped outside amid Xi’an Tower’s lavish send-off.

[P161]
The bustling streets of Xi’an were packed with people. Over the din, Baek Museong spoke.

[P162]
“I’d like to see you off, but you won’t allow it, will you?”

[P163]
“We’ll be seeing each other again later anyway.”

[P164]
“Haha. I knew you’d say that. Then I’ll be off. Stay well, Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”

[P165]
“Take care, Martial Nephew Baek!”

[P166]
In the end, I hadn’t even brought it up.

[P167]
Good. This was fine.

[P168]
Just as I was about to turn away, alone in my lingering unease amid the warm farewells, I overheard someone speaking.

[P169]
“Did you hear? The Taeeul Merciless Sword of the Zhongnan Sect is in Xi’an.”

[P170]
“What? The Taeeul Merciless Sword? Why on earth would he come here?”

[P171]
“How should I know? Someone saw him heading toward Tengwang Pavilion in the west. Apparently, he’s meeting with the Yongbong Escort Bureau… but I can’t say for sure.”

[P172]
The murmuring voices slowly faded into the distance.

[P173]
I turned to Cheongpung.

[P174]
“Young Master Cheongpung.”

[P175]
“Yes, Benefactor.”

[P176]
“Have you ever had tea?”

[P177]
“Yes! I have!”

[P178]
“No. You’ve never had tea.”

[P179]
If I said he hadn’t, then he hadn’t.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 317

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃317화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“아.”
  6|
  7|깜빡이는 긴 속눈썹 위로 햇살이 부서진다. 주화란은 잠에서 깬 후에도 침상에 누운 채 한참이나 천장을 바라보았다.
  8|
  9|어젯밤, 그녀와 용봉표국은 마침내 서안에 닿을 수 있었다.
 10|
 11|천력부가 이끄는 흑석채는 이번 표행의 마지막 장애물이었다.
 12|
 13|그들은 안전한 번화가를 지나 서안의 후미진 객잔에 행낭을 풀었다. 객잔에는 침상은 물론 따뜻한 음식과 목욕물이 모두를 기다리고 있었다.
 14|
 15|주화란은 모든 표물을 빠짐없이 점검한 다음 쓰러지듯 잠이 들었었다.
 16|
 17|‘드디어 끝이 보이는구나.’
 18|
 19|이곳은 안전하다. 산길을 막아서는 산적도, 정체를 숨기고 무리 지어 습격하던 낭인들도 없다. 이번 표행의 주목적이었던 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)을 종남파에 넘기기만 하면 끝이다.
 20|
 21|용봉표국은 노력에 합당한 보상을 받을 것이고 모두 함께 집으로 돌아갈 것이다.
 22|
 23|서른세 개의 유골함과 함께.
 24|
 25|‘서른셋…….’
 26|
 27|주화란의 눈동자가 문득 희미하게 깜빡였다.
 28|
 29|서른세 개의 유골함, 서른세 사람의 얼굴, 그들과 울고 웃었던 기억이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
 30|
 31|“아, 이러면 안 되는데…….”
 32|
 33|옷소매로 눈가를 문지른 주화란이 자신을 두 뺨을 강하게 쳤다. 짝! 하는 소리와 함께 흐트러진 정신이 조금이나마 돌아온다.
 34|
 35|“이제 시작이야. 정신 똑바로 차려야 해.”
 36|
 37|표행은 아직 끝나지 않았다.
 38|
 39|종남파와 약조한 기한까지는 사흘이 남았고, 그 안에 천년설삼을 무사히 전달해야만 표행이 끝난다.
 40|
 41|“그리고…… 새로운 시작이 되겠지.”
 42|
 43|주화란은 작은 목소리로 중얼거리며 품 안을 더듬었다. 단단히 밀봉된 목곽(木槨)을 꺼내어 확인한 뒤에 다시 집어넣어 끈으로 고정했다.
 44|
 45|단지 그것만으로도 시원한 향기가 코끝을 맴돌다가 이내 사라졌다.
 46|
 47|무림인이라면 누구나 바라마지 않는 천고의 영약, 천년설삼이 목곽 안에 들어 있었다.
 48|
 49|“흐트러지지 말자, 주화란. 이제 겨우 한 걸음이야.”
 50|
 51|주화란이 스스로를 향해 다짐하던 그때였다.
 52|
 53|“화란아, 일어났느냐?”
 54|
 55|문밖에서 들려온 익숙한 목소리. 옷매무새를 다듬은 주화란이 대답했다.
 56|
 57|“네, 허 숙부. 들어오셔도 돼요.”
 58|
 59|“그럼 잠시 실례하마.”
 60|
 61|잠시 후, 문을 열고 들어온 총표두 허준이 밝은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
 62|
 63|“예정보다 빨리 표국으로 돌아갈 수 있게 되었다.”
 64|
 65|“그 말씀은…….”
 66|
 67|“종남파가 서안에서 기다리고 있다는구나.”
 68|
 69|“종남파가요?”
 70|
 71|“그래. 그것도 태을무정검(太乙無情劍)이 직접 왔다고 들었다, 하하하.”
 72|
 73|웃음을 머금은 허준과는 달리, 주화란의 눈빛은 깊게 가라앉았다.
 74|
 75|‘종남파가, 그것도 태을무정검이 서안까지 직접?’
 76|
 77|귀환이 앞당겨졌으니 원래라면 허준처럼 기뻐해야 하는 것이 맞다.
 78|
 79|하지만 지금까지 종남파가 보여 온 오만무례한 태도를 생각할수록, 마음 깊숙한 곳에서 불안감이 스멀스멀 올라왔다.
 80|
 81|“허 숙부, 뭔가 이상하지 않아요?”
 82|
 83|“응? 이상하다니, 무엇이 말이냐?”
 84|
 85|“예정된 기간까지는 아직 사흘이나 남았어요.”
 86|
 87|“사흘밖에 안 남은 거지. 서안에서 종남산까지는 천천히 이동해도 이틀이면 충분하다.”
 88|
 89|“숙부께서 종종 그러셨죠. 무림에는 우연이 없다. 무슨 일이 벌어지더라도 이상하지 않은 곳이 무림이라고.”
 90|
 91|“화란아, 무슨 말이 하고 싶은 게냐?”
 92|
 93|도무지 이해가 되지 않는다는 듯한 허준의 눈빛에 주화란이 무겁게 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“지금까지 종남파는 우리 용봉표국을 은연중에 적대해 왔습니다. 이번 표행이 실패하는 걸 누구보다 원하고 있을 거예요. 일부러 어려운 조건을 내걸었던 이유도 그 때문이고요.”
 96|
 97|“하지만 받아들였지. 훌륭하게 해냈고.”
 98|
 99|종남파가 요구한 조건은 까다로운 것이었다. 오죽하면 종남파의 이름에 혹해서 몰려든 다른 표국주들조차 고개를 절레절레 내저으며 의뢰를 포기했을 정도다.
100|
101|그들이 원하는 기한 내에 천년설삼을 운송해 주지 못하면, 표행은 실패로 돌아가고 천문학적인 금액을 위약금으로 물어내야 하니까.
102|
103|하지만 주화란은 고심 끝에 종남파의 의뢰를 받아들였다.
104|
105|이유는 단 하나, 용봉표국의 비상(飛上)을 위해서였다.
106|
107|‘그리고 큰 희생을 치러야 했지.’
108|
109|일어나지 말아야 할 일이 일어났다.
110|
111|천년설삼에 관한 정보가 유출된 것이 원인이었다.
112|
113|주화란은 바보가 아니다. 아직은 경륜이 부족할 뿐, 모든 가능성을 열어 두고 생각할 줄 아는 명석한 두뇌의 소유자였다.
114|
115|지금까지 마음속에만 담아 두었던 의심이 서서히 실체를 갖추는 기분이다. 주화란은 조용히 입을 열었다.
116|
117|“어쩌면, 어쩌면 종남파가…….”
118|
119|“그만.”
120|
121|주화란의 말을 가로막은 허준의 얼굴은 딱딱하게 굳어 있었다.
122|
123|“그만하거라. 네가 지금 무슨 생각을 하고 있는지 모르는 바가 아니나, 그 이상은 터무니없다. 아니, 위험하기까지 해.”
124|
125|“하지만.”
126|
127|“종남파에 관한 소문은 익히 알고 있다. 그들이 자신들의 표국을 키우기 위해 우리를 견제하고 있다는 것도 사실이지. 하지만 지금 화란이 네가 말하려는 것은…… 위험한 억측이야.”
128|
129|“허 숙부…….”
130|
131|“숙부로서, 용봉표국의 총표두로서 부탁하마. 너와 표국을 위험에 빠트리지 말아라.”
132|
133|비록 피 한 방울 섞이지 않은 남이지만, 그녀의 어린 시절부터 늘 따뜻하게 대해 주었던 의숙부다.
134|
135|그런 그가 작심한 듯 굳은 얼굴로 말을 쏟아내자 주화란은 더 이상 종남파에 관한 말을 이을 수 없었다.
136|
137|“후우.”
138|
139|작게 한숨을 내쉬는 주화란의 어깨를 허준이 따뜻하게 감싸 안았다.
140|
141|“말이 심했다면 미안하구나.”
142|
143|“아니에요. 제가 좀 과민했나 봐요.”
144|
145|“그럴 만도 하지. 종남파가 안 하던 짓을 했으니. 당주나 총관도 아닌 태을무정검을 보낼 줄이야.”
146|
147|종남파 장문인의 두 사형 중 한 사람.
148|
149|늘 본산에 머무르며 두문불출하는 태을무정검을 사람들이 오랫동안 기억하는 이유는 간단했다.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
